data.title: Soybeans rally on rising Brazilian real, soymeal
data.description:
By Heather Schlitz

Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures rallied to a one-month high on Friday under support from a climbing Brazilian real, higher soymeal futures and a steady drip of export demand for US soybeans.

Corn and wheat futures also ticked higher under spillover support from soybeans.

Chicago Board of Trade January soybeans rose 22-1/4 cents to $12.66-1/4 a bushel, while March corn gained 6-1/2 cents to $4.63 per bushel.

Brazilian assets rallied ​on Friday after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva tapped a market-friendly bank executive to be his next finance ‌chief, following weeks of investor concern over the fiscal direction of the leftist leader's upcoming fourth term.

Export demand for soybeans has also been steady.

The US Department of Agriculture on Friday morning reported net weekly export sales of 755,800 metric tons of soybeans. The agency also reported a sale of 132,000 metric tons of soybeans to the Netherlands for 2026/2027 delivery in its daily reporting system on Friday morning.

Trade volume has been relatively light between Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday and the weekend. Grain markets were closed for Thanksgiving and traded for an abbreviated session on Friday.

Investors are weighing whether exports to China will be affected, as the top soy importer was already on pace to meet its annual purchasing commitment, while a disappointing harvest in South America could shift demand toward US soybeans.

The two countries are continuing to work on resolving agricultural trade issues.

The soy complex continued to receive support from soaring soymeal futures, which have continued to shoot higher on expectations that EU demand could rise due to the bloc's new deforestation rules that are set to take effect in late December.

CBOT March wheat settled 3-1/2 cents higher at $5.91 per bushel as traders assessed the ongoing conflict in the Black Sea.

Ukraine has offered a Black Sea ceasefire to enable food exports and passed this on to international allies, Kyiv's foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said on Friday.

data.title: TSLA Stock Clocks Best Week In 18 Months: Tesla Reportedly Eyes Buying German Toolmaker Amid Cybercab, Optimus Scaling Plans
data.description:
Key points:
  • EMAG designs and builds precision equipment for turning, grinding, and gear cutting, primarily serving the automotive industry. 
  • The company has also developed specialized systems for manufacturing high-precision gears used in humanoid robot actuators. 
  • Tesla, meanwhile, has begun early production of its Optimus humanoid robots at its production line at its Fremont factory.

Shares of EV giant Tesla (TSLA) rose on Friday, adding to a strong weekly performance, as the company reportedly plans to acquire Germany-based machine-tool maker EMAG.

TSLA stock started the short Thanksgiving week strong, thanks to a tech rally driven by the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO in less than two weeks of his ouster. The stock clocked small losses in the following two days, before jumping on Friday.

TSLA stock was up more than 5% at market close. It has gained nearly 16% overall this week, with anticipation for a deal between the company and SpaceX adding optimism, clocking its best week since May 2025, according to Koyfin data.

Tesla Eyes German Machine Maker

Tesla submitted plans to Germany’s competition authority without providing details of the transaction, Automotive World reported on Friday. The filing follows Tesla’s registration of Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE, a shell company renamed from an August entry, with its address at EMAG’s headquarters in Salach near Stuttgart, the report noted.

EMAG designs and builds precision equipment for turning, grinding, and gear cutting, primarily serving the automotive industry by producing machines that make drivetrain components such as transmissions and related parts. The company has also developed specialized systems for manufacturing high-precision gears used in humanoid robot actuators.

Deal Talks As Tesla Ramps Up Cybercab, Optimus Production

The news comes as Tesla has started early production of its Optimus humanoid robots at a production line at its Fremont factory, designed for up to one million units a year. On the third-quarter (Q3) earnings call, CEO Elon Musk reiterated that the hand of the robot is the main hardware challenge. The company is aiming to deliver the robots to external customers starting in late 2027.

Tesla’s sole European vehicle plant in Grünheide, Brandenburg, currently builds Model Y vehicles at roughly 375,000 annual capacity. The company recently announced a first €3 billion investment in the factory to produce up to one million Cybercab robotaxis a year there as well, with construction targeted for 2027 and production from 2029. Cybercab production is currently limited to the company’s factory in Texas.

How Did TSLA Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA stock stayed within ‘bullish’ territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at ‘low’ levels.

TSLA stock has dropped 11% year-to-date.

data.title: Athabasca Oil Corporation Announces Shareholder Approval of the Proposed Arrangement with Cenovus
data.description:
CALGARY, Alberta, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Athabasca Oil Corporation ("Athabasca" or the "Corporation") is pleased to announce that its proposed arrangement with Cenovus Energy Inc. ("Cenovus") (the "Transaction") was approved at today’s special meeting (the "Meeting") of holders of common shares of Athabasca.

At the Meeting, the special resolution (the "Transaction Resolution") approving the Transaction was approved by 98.84% of the votes cast by Athabasca shareholders, present in person (or virtually) or represented by proxy at the Meeting. For additional details of the voting results on the Transaction Resolution, see Athabasca's Report of Voting Results filed pursuant to Section 11.3 of National Instrument 51-102 – Continuous Disclosure Obligations available on Athabasca's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

Athabasca's application to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta (the "Court") for a final order in respect of the Transaction (the "Final Order") is expected to take place on December 1, 2026 and, subject to the approval of the Court and the satisfaction or waiver of other customary closing conditions, the Transaction is expected to close shortly thereafter.

Athabasca’s common shares will be delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange ("TSX") following the closing of the Transaction.

About Athabasca Oil Corporation

Athabasca Oil Corporation is a Canadian energy company with a focused strategy on the development of thermal and light oil assets. Situated in Alberta's Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin, the Corporation has amassed a significant land base of extensive, high quality resources. Athabasca's light oil assets are held in a private subsidiary (Duvernay Energy Corporation) in which Athabasca owns a 70% equity interest. Athabasca's common shares trade on the TSX under the symbol "ATH". For more information, visit www.atha.com.

For more information, please contact:

data.title: Crude Oil Slides As Trump Offers More Time For Diplomacy To Resolve Iran Crisis
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Crude oil prices have moved lower on Friday as near-term war concerns eased after U.S. President Donald Trump stated that he prefers to give Iran more opportunity to strike a deal with the U.S. However, supply concerns due to incidents of ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi-Saudi Arabia conflict restricted the decline.

WTI Crude Oil for January delivery was last seen trading down by $0.67 (or 0.80%) at $83.01 per barrel.

In his Thanksgiving address at his residence in Florida, Trump remarked that victory in the war with Iran would be achieved whenever he wants it.

Trump stated that he is giving another chance for Iran to act smart but he sounded skeptical if the present Iranian regime would utilize the offer. Trump wanted Iran to use this opportunity to decide wisely and save a lot of lives.

Re-asserting again that Iran can never be allowed to have a nuclear weapon, Trump warned that Iranian missiles can reach up to Europe.

Trump threatened that if no deal is reached with Iran, further U.S. attacks on Iran could even target the strategic Pickaxe Mountain where Iran is suspected of piling up enriched nuclear materials.

Though no signs of de-escalation has emerged, market participants are counting on the remarks by Trump last week when he stated that he preferred to wait and watch how negotiations with Iran unfolds until January 1.

Trump had stressed that he is not in any rush to take a decision on Iran.

Iraq is now seeking an allowance to raise its production capacity and quota baselines from the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries.

Iraq's oil minister Basim Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi stated that Iraq raised its oil exports to 3.60 million barrels per day.

Iraq is the second largest producer of the OPEC alliance. Al-Abadi added that Iraq is in discussions with major U.S. oil firms including ExxonMobil, Chevron, and ConocoPhillips regarding potential investments in several oilfields.

Reports indicate that the OPEC cartel will likely keep the production targets unchanged in its meeting on November 29.

Meanwhile, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps continued to announce incidents of ships hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz after they violated Iran's guidelines for navigation.

Iran's Fars news agency cited the IRGC as stating that while one oil tanker exploded, another tanker was forced to turn back. Reportedly, the two oil tankers attempted to secretly pass through an unauthorized route north of Ghavam Island.

While flows from the region picked up, global oil consumption has moved lower.

Late Thursday, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Qatar and Pakistan are carrying proposals between Iran and the U.S. Araghchi added that though Iran was reviewing several ideas presented before it, the nation stood by its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Aside from the U.S.-Iran standoff, the flare-up in the strikes between Saudi Arabia and Iran-supported Houthi militant group of Yemen renewed supply concerns.

The Houthis are targeting the oil-rich Kingdom of Saudi Arabia almost on a daily basis, targeting energy facilities, airports, and financial infrastructures in Riyadh.

Qatar strongly condemned the Houthi attacks and expressed full solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

In retaliation to the deadly Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, the Saudi Arabia led coalition fighting the group struck areas in Yemen.

According to energy experts, the release of a report on global oil demand outlook by Paris-based International Energy Agency on November 13, indicating an impending global supply glut is pressuring oil prices on the downside. The release highlighted that oil markets would shift back into a surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The U.S. dollar index was last seen trading at 104.04, up by 0.38 (or 0.37%) today.

data.title: Brazil leads LatAm higher as Lula taps Bradesco chairman for finance chief
data.description:
Key points:
  • MSCI LatAm stock index up 3.2%, FX up 2.3%
  • Trabuco appointment lifts Brazil assets
  • Copper gains place Chile on solid footing
  • EM bond outflows ease for second-straight week, JPM says

By Niket Nishant and Johann M Cherian

Most Latin American assets advanced on Friday, with the currencies index on track for its biggest weekly jump since August 2024, led by gains in Brazil after Bradesco Chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco was appointed as the country's finance chief.

The gains could help regional stocks recover some poise at the end of a tumultuous month marked by a global risk-off mood as concerns about the AI trade intensified.

MSCI's index of regional equities (.MILA00000PUS) added 3.2% and was on track for its biggest weekly gain in more than a month, while the corresponding currency gauge (.MILA00000CUS) rose 2.3%. Weekly gains for the currencies index were just short of advances seen last in late-October 2022.

Brazilian stocks rose as much as 4% as President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva tapped Trabuco, a market-friendly bank executive, to be his finance chief. Trabuco is expected to have a say in discussions over additional fiscal measures currently under consideration, an official said.

The index was last up 0.1%, limited by a 2.7% loss each in state-owned commodities companies Petrobras and Vale .

The real strengthened 2.2% versus the dollar and was set for its fifth consecutive day of gains, its longest winning streak since April. At 7.6%, it was poised for its strongest week since May 2020.

International bonds also gained broadly, with those maturing in 2054 (105756CJ7=) and 2050 (105756CB4=) up more than 2 cents on the dollar.

"The appointment is encouraging and reinforces our view that Brazil does not need everything to turn positive to rebound. Sustaining a re-rating, however, requires fiscal delivery and execution," Jefferies analysts said.

COPPER RALLY LIFTS CHILEAN ASSETS

Chilean stocks (.MMXIPSAGC) rose 1.7%, while the peso strengthened 1%. Price of copper, the country's top export item, rallied on Friday, posting its biggest gain since January.

Data from statistics agency INE showed unemployment rate hit 10% in the quarter through October, above the 9.8% expected by economists polled by Reuters.

Peruvian equities (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) rose 2.8% and the sol was up 0.2%.

"Peru remains one of our preferred structural stories, with relatively resilient growth despite lower commodity prices and El Nino driving near-term noise. Chile is more of a 2027-28 investment story," Jefferies said.

In Mexico, the stock index jumped 2% and the peso gained 0.2%. The economy posted a $2.1 billion trade surplus in October when adjusted for seasonal swings, the national statistics agency said.

Separately, Mexico filed a formal complaint with the United States over a US Drug Enforcement Administration tip line seeking information on suspected drug traffickers and allegedly corrupt Mexican officials, President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Friday.

Colombia's peso appreciated 1.6% and local stocks added 1.6%.

Emerging-market bond outflows eased for a second consecutive week, according to data from JP Morgan.

Elsewhere in EM, ratings agency Moody's upgraded Vietnam's sovereign credit rating to "Ba1" from "Ba2", citing improvements in institutional quality and the country's shift toward higher-value growth.

data.title: VisionWave Raises About $2 Million in Registered Offering With Resettable Warrants
data.description:
VisionWave closed a registered direct offering that generated approximately $2 million in gross proceeds, with investors purchasing common shares or pre-funded warrants paired with common warrants. The securities purchase agreement allows purchasers to buy up to an additional $2 million, while the warrants include a price reset subject to a $0.0475 floor. Aegis Capital acted as exclusive placement agent, and a separate waiver letter with YA II directs a substantial portion of offering and ATM proceeds toward covered debt.

data.title: How PrimeXBT’s TradingView Integration Helps Traders Navigate Always-on Crypto Markets

Bitcoin can move sharply overnight, during a weekend or while a trader is away from their screen. By the time they check the price again, a level they were watching may already have been broken.

That is why alerts, technical indicators and tools for testing strategies have become important for monitoring price movements, analysing volatility and making informed trading decisions. Early crypto exchanges generally offered basic charts and order books, which meant traders looking for more detailed analysis often had to use separate charting tools. Today, they can examine multiple timeframes, add technical indicators and set price alerts, while historical testing tools help them assess strategies against earlier market conditions.

Traders often follow several coins at once, and price alerts notify them when a market reaches a chosen level. Historical charts also show how a strategy performed during previous rallies and sell-offs. With hundreds of coins and a growing range of derivatives, screeners let traders scan by price move, volume and technical conditions.

TradingView brings these capabilities together in a single analytical environment. Used by more than 100 million traders and investors worldwide, the platform covers cryptocurrencies alongside shares, forex, commodities and indices, allowing traders to analyse different markets using the same tools.

data.title: FTC Release: Ten Additional States Join FTC Lawsuit Alleging Dollar General Charged Consumers More than Advertised for Many Products
data.description:
The Federal Trade Commission filed an amended complaint adding ten states as co-plaintiffs in a lawsuit alleging that Dollar General Corporation engaged in long-running deceptive pricing practices by routinely charging customers more at the register than the prices displayed on shelves, price tags and advertisements, costing consumers millions of dollars.

data.title: vVARDIS and Henry Schein One Launch One-Click Auto Charting for Early-Stage Cavity Care
data.description:
vVARDIS (), the Swiss healthcare company in the dental med-tech sector offering non-invasive treatment for early-stage cavities, and Henry Schein One, a global leader in dental technology, today announced the launch of clinical auto-charting functionality for clinicians documenting early-stage cavities.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261127771676/en/

When a clinician detects an early-stage cavity, auto-charting features in Dentrix and Ascend record the code in the patient's chart with one click, reducing the charting process by 86%. The care team can then choose Curodont® to treat the tooth during the same visit, without duplicate documentation and with access to patient education resources regarding Curodont® within the platform. Throughout this workflow, treatment planning and decisions remain solely at the discretion of the clinician and patient.

The launch will represent the next phase of the collaboration between vVARDIS and Henry Schein One, which earlier this year introduced in-software awareness of Curodont® Repair Fluoride Plus to practices that use Dentrix and Ascend across the United States.

Tooth decay is the world’s most prevalent non-communicable disease, affecting approximately 2.5 billion people globally.1 A recent population-based cohort study in the U.S. associates untreated cavities with a 26 percent increased risk of all-cause mortality and a 48 percent increase in heart-disease mortality.2 Curodont® is designed as a non-invasive treatment intended to arrest or reverse early-stage cavities without drilling. Since its U.S. commercial launch in January 2024, vVARDIS estimates that Curodont® Repair Fluoride Plus has been used to treat over 3.5 million teeth and has been sold to over 20,000 of the approximately 110,000 general dental practices in the U.S., as of June 30, 2026.3

"Finding an early cavity and treating it should be one workflow, not two," said Haley Abivardi, DMD, co-CEO and co-founder of vVARDIS. “Dental teams want accurate information about their options for early-stage cavities, and patients want to understand the treatment they receive. This new functionality is another example of how technology is helping to create more efficiency in dental practices.”

"Our vision for Dentrix and Ascend is to bring intelligence directly into the clinical workflow, supporting clinicians without adding complexity. Auto-charting for the treatment of early-stage cavities is a great example of how we are connecting clinical insights, AI imaging, and documentation in a one click workflow to make technology work more simply for the dental team,” said April Lowry, Executive Director and General Manager, Clinical and AI, Henry Schein One.

This partnership promises to streamline access to drill-free dental solutions for patients across the United States.

“Dentrix and Ascend are part of the daily workflow for tens of thousands of U.S. practices,” said Greg Smith, Senior Vice President and General Manager, North America, vVARDIS. “We’re pleased to work with Henry Schein One to make information about Curodont® and drill-free treatment options for early-stage cavities more accessible to dental practices.”

Availability

Dentrix and Ascend are used in more than 75,000 locations in the United States. Auto-charting and the in-software Curodont® content are expected to become available within the next 30 days. vVARDIS and Henry Schein One plan to demonstrate the integration at the Greater New York Dental Meeting in New York City, November 29 to December 2, 2026.

About vVARDIS

vVARDIS () is a Swiss healthcare company in the dental med-tech sector headquartered in Zug, Switzerland, founded by Drs. Haley and Goly Abivardi, sisters, internationally renowned dentists and serial entrepreneurs. The company’s proprietary Curodont® technology platform offers an early therapeutic solution for tooth decay. Its flagship products are based on proprietary, peptide-containing formulations that complement the patient’s natural biology to help it stop the progression of early-stage cavities, preserve natural tooth structure and repair damaged enamel in early-stage cavities. Curodont®’s underlying technology is supported by a body of scientific evidence accumulated over the last 25 years, published in more than 250 publications, including randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses and long-term real-world cohort analyses. Curodont® is featured in the curricula of over 50 U.S. and European dental programs. For more information, visit www.vVARDIS.com and ww.linkedin.com/company/vvardis.

About Henry Schein One

Henry Schein One, a global leader in dental technology, empowers dentists to focus on patient care and helps to ensure practice success. With simple and integrated technology, practices become more efficient, profitable, and connected—leading to better experiences for patients and care teams alike. The company’s comprehensive portfolio spans demand generation, patient experience, practice management, revenue cycle, analytics, and clinical workflow.

Henry Schein One, LLC, is a joint venture between Henry Schein, Inc. () and Internet Brands. Its brands include Dentrix, Ascend by Dentrix, Jarvis Analytics, TechCentral, Lighthouse360, and DentalPlans.com, as well as international brands such as Dentally and Software of Excellence.

data.title: Precious Metals Rally as AI Trade Revives Risk Appetite — Update
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni and Adam Whittaker

Precious-metal prices surged Friday as investors returned to the artificial-intelligence trade and global stocks rebounded, boosting risk appetite and easing pressure on assets that had been sold to meet liquidity needs.

Copper futures rose 3.4% Friday to $5.5170 a pound.

The rally also lifted mining stocks in London, with the sector leading gains on the FTSE 100. Friday's advance follows a challenging period for mining companies, whose shares have come under pressure as metal prices weakened and concerns about the AI trade weighed on investor sentiment.

Silver and gold miner Fresnillo shares rose 4.8%, while its peer Endeavour Mining gained 3.1%. Copper producer Antofagasta climbed 4.4%. Diversified miners Glencore and Anglo American, both with significant exposure to copper, advanced 4.3% and 3.8%, respectively. Valterra Platinum's London-listed shares gained 7.8%.

"Beyond the technical nature of the rebound, the recovery also highlights the role of precious metals as an ATM in times of market stress," analysts at Saxo Bank said. "With AI-related technology stocks rebounding and broader risk appetite improving, the queue at the cash machine appears to be thinning, easing the liquidity-driven selling pressure."

Still, the broader macroeconomic backdrop remains challenging. Traders are pricing in a quarter-point rate hike at the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting in December, while attention is also turning to whether the U.S. central bank will signal further monetary tightening for 2027.

Higher interest rates can weigh on nonyielding assets such as gold and silver by making interest-bearing investments relatively more attractive.

data.title: SpaceX Stocks Climb 2.74% as FCC Clears One Million AI Satellites
data.description:
SpaceX shares climbed 2.74% to $130.94 at 10:35 a.m. ET on Friday, November 27, extending a rebound after the Federal Communications Commission authorized up to one million Starmind AI data-center satellites. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr announced the approval on November 25.

Starmind is SpaceX's bet that AI compute can move into orbit, with the first launch targeted for the third quarter of 2027 on Starship. The shares still trade below the $135 IPO price from June and far from the first-week peak of $225.64, according to Finexus, which also reported Elon Musk's pledge to give one Class A share a year to each American child with a Trump Account. Anthropic's prospectus puts its potential monthly AI bill with SpaceX at about $3.1 billion, 24/7 Wall St. reported on Friday.

The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 21/100, with very weak profitability the main drag, which is typical for a company spending ahead of revenue. That makes the $1.78 trillion valuation a bet on new lines of business rather than current earnings. If Anthropic's bill reached $3.1 billion a month, it would equal about $37 billion a year from one customer, a concrete anchor for the orbital compute story. The next test is Starship's launch cadence through 2027, since every Starmind satellite depends on it.

data.title: Palantir Stocks Climb 3.72% on $300 Million Poland Defense AI Deal
data.description:
Palantir Technologies shares climbed 3.72% to $169.67 at 10:35 a.m. ET on Friday, November 27, after Poland signed a five-year deal worth roughly $300 million for its AI-enabled software. The country's defense minister confirmed the value, Seeking Alpha reported.

The contract covers AI software for Poland's defense and security infrastructure, MyAllies News reported on Friday. Spread evenly, $300 million over five years works out to about $60 million a year. Measured against the rally, the gap is striking: a 3.72% gain on a market value near $409 billion added roughly $14.7 billion, about 49 times the contract's total value.

The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 85/100, with a strong balance sheet and momentum but a profitability reading that lags the rest of the scorecard. The GF Value of $227.99 implies a 25.6% discount, which GuruFocus calls modestly undervalued. The market reaction shows investors are paying for the European pipeline the deal signals, not the deal itself. The next test is whether other NATO defense ministries follow Poland with signed contracts of their own.

data.title: Alibaba Stocks Climb 4.38% as Beijing Calls on State Funds to Steady Markets
data.description:
Alibaba Group shares climbed 4.38% to $90.03 at 10:35 a.m. ET on Friday, November 27, after Beijing pledged stronger support for its equity markets. Following a State Council meeting, Xinhua said Central Huijin would strengthen its role as a quasi-stabilization fund, and margin-lending rules were relaxed, Reuters reported.

Mainland markets reacted hard: the CSI300 rose 4.2%, the STAR 50 jumped 15% and its semiconductor sub-index posted a record 19% gain. The cabinet also pushed listed companies to raise dividends and buybacks, and Alibaba's Hong Kong shares rose 5% to HK$86.6. Investing.com noted that southbound investors bought HK$1.267 billion of Alibaba on the day, while Susquehanna cut its target to $145 from $190 but kept a positive rating.

The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 79/100: solid profitability and balance sheet, but momentum is among the weakest readings on the board after a slide from the $181 range. The GF Value of $123.65 implies a 27.2% discount, which GuruFocus calls modestly undervalued; China policy rallies have faded before, so that gap becomes a value case only if buybacks actually grow. The next measurable test is Alibaba's next buyback disclosure, and whether its chip unit delivers on plans to mass-produce the Zhenwu V900 in the first quarter of 2027.

data.title: Micron Stocks Climb 4.29% as Chip Rebound Meets Tight 2027 Memory Supply
data.description:
Micron Technology shares climbed 4.29% to $627.04 at 10:35 a.m. ET on Friday, November 27, as chip shares rebounded in the shortened post-Thanksgiving session. Even after the bounce, the memory maker sits about 48% below its record close of $1,213.56 from June 25, a drawdown that clashes with management's supply outlook.

Speaking in Austin on November 18, CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said memory supply in 2027 and 2028 will be even tighter than in 2026, and that Micron is already discussing 2028 volumes with customers. The company has signed 26 strategic customer agreements, many running five years on take-or-pay terms, backed by $32 billion in upfront cash and financial commitments. Mehrotra also ranked factories ahead of shareholder returns, citing more than $250 billion of planned U.S. manufacturing investment.

The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 96/100, built on a strong balance sheet and high profitability. The GF Value of $867.88 implies a 27.8% discount, which GuruFocus labels modestly undervalued. The $32 billion of commitments equals about 4.5% of Micron's $710 billion market value, small against the equity but meaningful as a floor under 2027 revenue. The next test is Micron's next quarterly report, where investors will look for whether contract pricing holds into 2027.

data.title: Yields rise as tech stocks extend rebound
data.description:
By Colin Barr

US Treasury yields rose on Friday, reflecting the latest shift in investor sentiment on the AI buildout that in recent months has swamped other dynamics in global markets.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose 8.6 basis points to 4.93% and the 2-year yield (US2YT=RR), more sensitive to expectations for Federal Reserve policy, rose 7.3 bps to 4.71%. The 10-year yield is essentially flat for the month, reflecting tension between expectations that the Fed will raise rates multiple times in coming months to tamp down inflation and investor fear that the unwind of the artificial intelligence trade could tighten financial conditions enough to hit consumer spending and slow growth.

On Friday, US stocks rose, extending the gains they made late on Wednesday after the Nasdaq 100 briefly fell 20% from its high last month. The Nasdaq Composite rose 2.3% and the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX added 1.6%. Pullbacks that push markets near so-called bear market territory have frequently triggered strong rebounds in recent years, reflecting a buy-the-dip mentality that has broadly paid off for investors ever since the recovery from the 2008 financial crisis.

"Financial conditions are once again in focus in light of the dramatic swings in the US equity market," said Ian Lyngen, managing director and head of US rates strategy at BMO Capital Markets in New York.

"Stability would be a welcome reprieve in light of the performance of risk assets in recent weeks, although we’re not convinced that the tech sector has fully repriced to the array of uncertainties facing the AI buildout."

The US yield curve is now at its flattest since early last year, said Jonas Goltermann, chief markets economist at Capital Economics. While there is some debate about how much signal there actually is in this indicator, Goltermann warns that "high short-term yields relative to long-term ones reflect a judgment among market participants that tight monetary policy will weigh on economic growth – and corporate earnings – further ahead."

Investors next will focus on next week's nonfarm payrolls report on Friday, just days before the December Fed meeting. Few expect the jobs report to reduce the pressure on the central bank to act at the coming meeting and the ones that follow it, Lyngen said in his weekly rates report.

"Our base case remains 25 bp hikes at the next three meetings (Dec, Jan, Mar), followed by an extended period on hold during 2027 as the Fed awaits the impact of a tighter policy stance," Lyngen said.

He said BMO remains bullish on Treasury investments and expects that stance to become even more constructive "once there are signs of strain within the real economy – a facet of the current stage of the cycle that has been conspicuously absent."

data.title: Samsung Electronics Stocks Jump 4.55% as Seoul Rallies on Stabilization Hopes
data.description:
Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) shares jumped 4.55% to 179,100 won at the November 27 regular-session close in Seoul, riding a 4.34% rally in the KOSPI. Bargain hunters returned after a week of doubts over the AI trade, and Yonhap reported that financial authorities plan to expand a market stabilization fund.

Trade news helped as well. TokenPost tied the rally to easing tariff concerns after Washington proposed duties of up to 15% on Taiwanese goods while proposing an exemption for chips and chip equipment, a template Korean chipmakers would welcome. Samsung beat the index but trailed SK hynix's 5.41% gain, a gap that likely reflects the market's preference for the HBM leader. The KOSPI finished at 4,915.68, up 204.47 points.

The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 96/100, anchored by a top-rated balance sheet and strong profitability. The GF Value of 199,414.43 won implies a 10.2% discount, which GuruFocus calls modestly undervalued, so the policy bounce has not used up the model's upside. At about 1,117 trillion won, Samsung's market value is roughly 1.5 times SK hynix's, yet the smaller rival has arguably been the cleaner AI memory story this year. The next test is whether Seoul's stabilization measures arrive with real money behind them.

data.title: SA Asks: What's the best gold play right now for investors?
data.description:
What's the best gold play right now for investors?

Seeking Alpha analysts Andrew Hecht, Brett Aschcroft Green, and Eugenio Catone weigh in.

Andrew Hecht: Gold is ugly, along with other markets that appear to be undergoing a risk-off phase. Picking bottoms is dangerous, as prices can fall to unreasonable, illogical, and irrational levels before finding bottoms.

All the analysts who were forecasting prices at $6,000 earlier this year again have egg on their face. Remember, they were the same analysts who never forecast gold reaching the level it rose to in late January 2026.

While I still believe gold will find a higher low, the next long-term support is the psychological $3,000 level. However, technical support for the bull market that began in 1999 is at the December 2023 high of $2,130.20 per ounce, more than $1,385 below last Friday's settlement price on Nov. 20. Central banks will continue to add to reserves at lower prices. That said, sentiment has taken a significant hit as gold has fallen by more than $2,000 per ounce from the Jan. 29, 2026, record high.

As a long-term investor, I would add to long positions by buying physical gold or SPDR Gold Shares ETF , the most liquid gold ETF that holds physical gold bullion. In late November 2026, gold and all precious metals remain falling knives, so be careful.

(Andrew Hecht leads the SA investing group The Hecht Commodity Report.)

Brett Aschcroft Green: The recent sell-off in gold could create an opportunity, as the metal may eventually represent a flight-to-safety asset and could be boosted by rate cuts if inflation subsides. I recently covered a few metals funds, which included a physical gold ETF, the SPDR Gold Shares ETF ; a large-cap miner fund, the VanEck Gold Miners ETF ; and a junior miner fund, the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF .

In the event of a sell-off, I’d be more inclined to go with the actual metals rather than the mining stocks.

Eugenio Catone: As I expressed in a recent article, the AI sell-off has led investors to sell liquid assets like gold to face margin calls. Since leverage is still high in the financial system, I expect a further drop in gold prices, at least until $3,400 per ounce, which is where the next strong volumetric support lies.

So, in my opinion, the best play here is to just wait until the dust settles ($3,400 per ounce) and buy a liquid ETC on gold for the long term. In this period, I would avoid miners as they are subject to operating leverage, something that becomes a major headwind when gold is in a sharp downward trend.

data.title: Bitcoin whales pile into BTC despite shrinking profit cushion
data.description:
Bitcoin whales are bucking the years-long trend of trimming their balances toward the end of the year. Instead, they are accumulating the cryptocurrency despite falling prices and dwindling unrealized profits.

According to onchain analytics firm CryptoQuant, whales added about 121,000 Bitcoin to their holdings between Sept. 30 and Nov. 21, taking their combined balance to nearly 2.95 million BTC, despite a price decline of nearly 30% over the same period.

CryptoQuant defines whales as addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC. Unrealized profits across addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have shrunk 81% to $23.8 billion from $124.7 billion on Sept. 30.

The report, supported by crypto lending platform CoinRabbit, notes that whales have historically reduced their holdings toward the end of the year in both bull and bear markets. Since 2017, whale balances have declined in seven of the nine previous fourth quarters, with 2019 and 2020 being the only exceptions.

Meanwhile, dolphins, a term referring to addresses holding between 100 and 1,000 BTC, have slightly reduced their holdings. The group shed about 15,169 BTC, representing 0.28% of its holdings.

Bitcoin loans may be taking the place of sales

The accumulation comes as Bitcoin has lost about 32% of its value since the beginning of the year, with the cryptocurrency trading at around $59,750 at 6:45 p.m. UTC on Friday, according to TradingView data. The report notes that borrowing against Bitcoin holdings may be allowing some large investors to access liquidity without selling their assets.

According to CryptoQuant, among CoinRabbit users with more than $100,000 in loans, the number of Bitcoin-backed loans increased by 298.9% month-on-month in October, while total loan volume fell by 16.2%.

The pattern contrasts with October 2025, when the number of Bitcoin-backed loans fell by 3.7% but total loan volume increased by 122.8%.

CryptoQuant suggested that the shift toward more frequent but smaller loans could indicate that large holders are borrowing to raise cash instead of selling Bitcoin.

Crypto tax firm Summ suggested the shift could also be linked to the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). Since January, participating jurisdictions have begun requiring crypto exchanges and other service providers to collect users’ transaction data for tax authorities, with the first international exchanges of tax-related information expected in 2027.

Summ CEO Shane Brunette said holding BTC and borrowing against it are rational responses “to a world where every sale is visible.”

data.title: Apple faces countersuit from OpenAI for stealing trade secrets - FT
data.description:
OpenAI has launched a new legal action against Apple , accusing the iPhone maker of stealing trade secrets and blocking access to hardware suppliers, reported the Financial Times on Friday.

OpenAI filed the lawsuit in a California court on Friday, according to the report.

OpenAI claimed that Apple is using its “size and wealth to forestall competition,” including threatening suppliers that might work on its new devices, alleging a “wide variety of unlawful, unfair, and tortious conduct,” the Financial Times report added.

The ChatGPT maker and Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comments.

The report also stated that OpenAI accused Apple of “coercing and threatening” suppliers that are also working with the ChatGPT maker.

OpenAI also reportedly said that one of its former employees who returned to Apple shared details about its product plans and suppliers. According to the Financial Times, OpenAI claimed that Apple encouraged its employees to store corporate files on their personal devices and cloud storage accounts.

The new development comes after Apple, in July, reportedly sent legal letters to former employees who now work for OpenAI, with the tech giant alleging that OpenAI is stealing trade secrets.

Apple alleged OpenAI used former and current Apple employees to steal confidential hardware designs and confidential information of unreleased technologies, processes and products. It also alleges that the misconduct was orchestrated by OpenAI's leadership.

Last year, OpenAI also acquired io, the AI startup led by Apple’s former design chief Sir Jony Ive, for $6.4 billion, creating a new source of tension between the two companies.

The continuing legal battle will further deteriorate the relationship between the two companies, who once partnered in June 2024 to integrate ChatGPT into iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. Apple also worked with OpenAI to help upgrade its Siri assistant.

data.title: Dollar set for weekly gain as risk appetite returns
data.description:
Key points:
  • Australian dollar rebounds from Wednesday's near one-year low as sentiment improves
  • China's steps to support equities add to broader market risk appetite
  • Fed funds futures imply near-certain December hike and sizable odds of another in January

By Karen Brettell

Improving risk appetite on Friday bolstered risk-sensitive currencies including the Australian dollar, while the US dollar was on track for a modest weekly gain.

Wall Street's main indexes ended higher on Friday and posted weekly gains as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday and flocked to hard-hit AI-linked shares. Efforts by China to shore up its stock market also boosted sentiment.

"A dip-buying recovery in tech stocks is lifting risk appetite across markets," said Elias Haddad, global head of markets strategy at Brown Brothers Harriman.

The US currency has benefited from safe-haven demand amid volatile equity markets, but it is also sensitive to capital flows to the AI trade, which has made it difficult at times to parse market moves.

“FX markets have shaken off their fixation on energy markets, replacing it, for now, with a focus on equities,” said Daragh Maher, head of digital assets research and senior FX strategist at HSBC.

“This creates a headache. The USD’s relationship with equities is unreliable, caught between its safe-haven role and its appeal as a proxy for US exceptionalism. The same equity signal could prompt very different FX responses,” he said.

The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.25% to 104.04, with the euro down 0.31% at $1.0933. The US currency is headed for a weekly gain of 0.2%.

The Australian dollar strengthened 0.18% versus the greenback to $0.6644, recovering from an almost one-year low reached on Wednesday.

FED TO CONTINUE HIKING

With US growth remaining strong and inflation still elevated, traders are pricing in continued rate hikes from the Federal Reserve, which has also supported the US currency.

Fed funds futures traders are pricing in 99% odds of a hike in December and a 64% chance of an additional increase in January, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool.

Key data releases next week, including November’s jobs report, will be evaluated for further clues on likely Fed policy.

Data on Friday showed that the US trade deficit in goods widened sharply in October as an AI infrastructure buildout boosted imports to a record high, potentially putting trade on course to again subtract from economic growth in the fourth quarter.

DOLLAR/YEN 160 LEVEL BACK IN FOCUS

Against the Japanese yen , the dollar strengthened 0.16% to 159.51, amid concerns about another round of Japanese intervention.

Data showed that annual core inflation in Tokyo accelerated in November at the fastest pace in 16 months, bolstering the case for an interest rate hike as soon as next month.

"The yen is understandably weaker today given the strong rebound in risk that has helped lift US Treasury bond yields," said Derek Halpenny, strategist at MUFG. "Better risk conditions could quickly bring back focus on intervention, especially if we get a hawkish hike from the FOMC on December 9."

In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 1.38% to $59,922.
